newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: United Overseas Land sees better 1997.
newsitem.headline: United Overseas Land sees better 1997.

text.p: United Overseas Land Ltd said on Friday it expected better 1997 results due mainly to contributions from its hotel investments in Australia.

The company said in a statement accompanying its results that the hotel industry in Singapore would continue to consolidate following a slowdown in visitor arrivals growth and the new supply of hotel rooms and service apartments in 1996.
"In contrast the outlook of the hotel industry in Australia remains positive and will contribute to the earnings of the group," it said.
Demand for office space in Singapore was expected to be sustained but new supply could put pressure on rental rates and capital values, it said.
Sentiment in the residential property market remained cautious after the introduction of anti-speculation measures last May.
UOL reported a 27 percent increase in profit to Singapore $64.43 million for year ended December 31, 1996. Turnover rose by 34 percent to S$311.7 million.

The company said the higher turnover was a result of the inclusion of revenue from its Westwood Park development in Singapore and the full year's contribution from its Landmark Parkroyal and Sheraton Perth Hotel, which were acquired in 1995. -- Singapore newsroom (65-8703080)
